record.original_question: For standard, join-style conditional term-rewriting systems whose rules have the form p implies l rewrites to r and whose conditions require terms to be joinable, is unicity of normal forms a modular property?

evidence.quote: Is unicity of normal forms a modular property of standard conditional systems?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A term-rewriting system (TRS) over a signature $\mathcal{F}$ and a denumerable set of variables consists of a set of rewrite rules. A standard join-style conditional term-rewriting system (CTRS) is a set of conditional rewrite rules of the form
$$ s_1 \downarrow t_1,\ \dots,\ s_n \downarrow t_n \;\Longrightarrow\; l \to r, $$
where $l,r,s_i,t_i$ are terms, $l$ is not a variable, every variable of $r$ and of the conditions occurs in $l$, and the relation $s\downarrow t$ holds iff there exists a term $u$ with $s \to^{*} u$ and $t \to^{*} u$ in the rewrite relation induced by the system. A normal form is a term to which no rule applies. A TRS is said to have unique normal forms (UN) if no term rewrites to two distinct normal forms (equivalently, every $\to^{*}$-equivalent pair of normal forms is identical, in the join formulation: any two normal forms reachable from a common term coincide).

Two CTRSs $\mathcal{R}_1$ over $\mathcal{F}_1$ and $\mathcal{R}_2$ over $\mathcal{F}_2$ are said to be disjoint if $\mathcal{F}_1 \cap \mathcal{F}_2 = \emptyset$. A property $P$ of CTRSs is called modular (over disjoint unions) if, whenever $\mathcal{R}_1$ and $\mathcal{R}_2$ are disjoint CTRSs both having $P$, their disjoint union $\mathcal{R}_1 \cup \mathcal{R}_2$ also has $P$.

Question: Is unique normal forms (UN) a modular property of standard join-conditional term-rewriting systems? That is, do there exist disjoint join-CTRSs $\mathcal{R}_1$ and $\mathcal{R}_2$, each satisfying UN, whose disjoint union does not satisfy UN, or does UN always transfer to the disjoint union?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been resolved in the negative: Kai Scheffermann constructed a counterexample showing that unicity of normal forms is not a modular property for join conditional term-rewriting systems, in contrast with Middeldorp's earlier positive modularity result for semi-equational CTRSs.

status_evidence.title: A Counterexample to the Modularity of Unicity of Normal Forms for Join Conditional Term Rewriting Systems
status_evidence.snippet: A counterexample showing UN is not modular for join CTRSs.
status_evidence.claim: UN is not a modular property of join conditional term rewriting systems.

status_evidence.title: Modular Properties of Conditional Term Rewriting Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Modularity results (and limits) for conditional term rewriting systems, including UN for semi-equational CTRSs.
status_evidence.claim: UN is modular for semi-equational CTRSs, motivating the join-CTRS question.
